rules.title: Massachusetts security deposit law (G.L. c. 186, § 15B)
rules.requirement: A security deposit may not exceed the first month's rent. It must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, with a receipt giving the bank details within 30 days. The lessor must give a signed deposit receipt and a statement of condition within 10 days of the tenancy start or of receipt, whichever is later. Interest of 5% per year, or the lesser amount the bank paid, is due to the tenant annually. The deposit or balance must be returned within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Deductions are limited to unpaid rent or water charges, unpaid tax escalations, and reasonable damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, supported by a sworn itemized list. The lessor must keep deposit records for 2 years. Deposits transfer to a successor in interest, who must give notice within 45 days. Violations forfeit the right to retain the deposit and carry treble damages. Lease terms that waive these rights are void. As amended effective August 1, 2025, regulations may allow an optional fee in lieu of a deposit, capped at 1 month's rent in total.
rules.key_value: Deposit max 1 month's rent; return within 30 days after tenancy ends; 5% annual interest (or lesser bank rate); 3x deposit plus 5% interest, court costs and attorney's fees for violations; fee in lieu of deposit capped at 1 month's rent combined with any deposit

rules.title: Massachusetts limit on upfront payments at or before tenancy start (G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b))
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, a lessor or its agent may not require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay more than: first full month's rent; last full month's rent at the same rate; a security deposit of no more than the first month's rent; and the purchase and installation cost of a key and lock. After the tenancy starts, the lessor may not demand rent in advance beyond the current month or a deposit above the statutory limit. No interest or penalty for late rent may be charged until 30 days after the rent is due. An optional fee in lieu of a deposit may be authorized by regulation, capped at 1 month's rent in total.
rules.key_value: Upfront charges limited to first month, last month, deposit up to 1 month's rent, and lock/key cost; no late-rent interest or penalty until 30 days after due

result.doc_summary: Official text of Massachusetts G.L. c. 186, § 15B, showing both the pre-August 1, 2025 and amended versions. It limits upfront charges at tenancy start to first month's rent, last month's rent, a deposit of up to one month's rent, and a key/lock cost. It requires deposits to be held in separate interest-bearing accounts with receipts, a statement of condition, 5% annual interest and return within 30 days. It restricts deductions and provides treble damages and forfeiture for violations. It also covers successor-in-interest transfers and the optional fee in lieu of a deposit added in 2025. Vacation rentals of 100 days or less are exempt.
